root_cause.text: The AMDGPU_INFO_READ_MMR_REG handler acquired the reset semaphore (via down_read_trylock) before performing memory allocation and copy_to_user, leading to potential deadlocks and incorrect locking order.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message explicitly identifies these issues: "the order between the reset semaphore and the mm_lock was wrong (e.g. copy_to_user) was called while holding the lock" and "we allocated memory while holding the reset semaphore which is also a pretty big bug and can deadlock" and "we used down_read_trylock() instead of waiting for the reset to finish." The patch moves the down_read after memory allocation, changes to down_read (waiting), and moves the up_read before copy_to_user.

candidates.rationale: Acquires the reset semaphore before memory allocation and copy_to_user, creating a large atomic context that can lead to deadlocks if those operations trigger reclaim or page faults that also need the semaphore.
Immediate return when lock is not acquired; though not the core vulnerability, it is part of the locking pattern that precedes the problematic operations.
Memory allocation performed while holding the reset semaphore; kmalloc with GFP_KERNEL may trigger reclaim that could try to acquire the same semaphore, causing a deadlock.
copy_to_user performed while holding the reset semaphore; a page fault during the copy may attempt to acquire the same semaphore, leading to a deadlock.
Releases the reset semaphore after the vulnerable operations; the entire window from acquisition to release includes blocking operations that cause the vulnerability.
Evaluates the result of copy_to_user while still holding the reset semaphore; this is part of the atomic section that should be minimized.
Frees allocated memory while holding the reset semaphore; kfree can trigger memory reclaim that might contend for the same lock, contributing to the deadlock risk.

The "alloc_size" calculation can overflow leading to memory corrupt
bic_trace_step.code_snippet:
commit 0d2edd3791bb172a59d708d5c94330bbd6050f97
Author: Dan Carpenter <error27@gmail.com>
Date:   Wed Sep 23 14:00:12 2015 +0300

    drm/amdgpu: integer overflow in amdgpu_info_ioctl()
    
    The "alloc_size" calculation can overflow leading to memory corruption.
    
    Reviewed-by: Christian König <christian.koenig@amd.com>
    Reported-by: Ilja Van Sprundel <ivansprundel@ioactive.com>
    Signed-off-by: Dan Carpenter <dan.carpenter@oracle.com>
    Signed-off-by: Alex Deucher <alexander.de
bic_trace_step.reason: In the AMDGPU_INFO_READ_MMR_REG case (lines 392-425), line 412 computes alloc_size using the expression `info->read_mmr_reg.count * sizeof(*regs)` without any overflow protection. This multiplication can overflow when count is large, leading to an incorrect alloc_size value used in the copy_to_user call (line 423). The earlier kmalloc_array (line 409) safely checks for overflow, but the separate alloc_size calculation does not, leaving the vulnerability present. No fix (e.g., casting to size_t or using a safe multiplication) is applied in this commit.
